description: Mammal Study explores the animals most like us: what makes a mammal, how animals are classified, studying mammals in the field, tracks, photography and museums, a project that helps mammal populations, outdoor ethics, and careers.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. The 2026 update added a careers option as requirement 7 and changed the size of the study area in one option of requirement 3; the official web page and the change notice disagreed on the size, so check the current text.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: What a mammal is
requirements.summary: Animals, invertebrates, vertebrates and mammals, and what sets mammals apart.

requirements.title: Classification
requirements.summary: How the animal kingdom is classified, from phylum to species.

requirements.title: Field study
requirements.summary: One option: studying mammals in two habitats, in one small area over several days, or a life history.

requirements.title: Learning about mammals
requirements.summary: One option, such as photographing mammals, a tracking pit, a museum visit or a book report.

requirements.title: A mammal project
requirements.summary: A project that affects the numbers of one or more kinds of mammals.

requirements.title: Outdoor ethics
requirements.summary: Leave No Trace and the Outdoor Code as they apply to mammal study.

requirements.title: Careers or hobbies
requirements.summary: One option, including a career related to mammals.
